dedupe_keys.name: grocery gap atlas food access scores and grocery store ownership concentration for us census tracts counties and states

description: The Grocery Gap Atlas maps how easily people across the United States can reach grocery stores and how concentrated grocery ownership is. RAFI-USA built it with the University of Chicago, and the data page documents its sources and methods. Store locations come from InfoGroup Reference USA (Data Axle) records coded as grocery stores, warehouse stores, supercentres and some dollar stores, weighted by sales volume, with corporate ownership, combined with American Community Survey population, census tract centroids, residential segregation and area deprivation indices. Food access scores use a gravity model with a floating catchment area built with the PySAL access module, reported as percentiles for census tracts and as population-weighted averages for counties and states. Coverage is the United States with data accessed between January and May 2024. The atlas is a free web map and data page. Caveats: some stores carry old names or are miscoded inside plazas, distances are straight-line, not road travel, the underlying store file is commercial so raw locations are not redistributed, and the licence for derived scores is not stated. Simulation uses: identifying food access deserts for disruption scenarios, weighting populations by grocery dependence, and testing how store closures or market concentration affect access. Related records: Map the Meal Gap (data-feeding-america-map-the-meal-gap) gives county food insecurity and the USDA SNAP retailer locator (data-usda-snap-retailer-locator) lists retailers.
